name: Reverse Rule Classification and Ambiguity Audit

classificationVocabulary.DIRECT_REVERSAL_CANDIDATE: Unique single-cell character rule with no detected segmentation overlap. Candidate only; not yet normative reverse semantics.
classificationVocabulary.STATE_OR_POLICY_REQUIRED: Cell signature collides with another forward rule and requires parser state, context, or explicit output policy.
classificationVocabulary.PARSER_RULE_REQUIRED: Non-colliding rule that still requires sequence/context/mode or multi-cell parser treatment.
classificationVocabulary.STRUCTURAL_RECONSTRUCTION_REQUIRED: Forward rule emits no Braille cells; reverse behavior must be defined by structural/layout/normalization reconstruction policy.

architectureImplications: Reverse translation cannot be implemented as a global Braille-cell lookup table.
The reverse engine needs explicit parser state for numeric and Latin modes plus capitalization.
Numeric mode does not identify which print digit family (ASCII, Persian, Arabic-Indic) should be emitted; Phase 13 needs an explicit output policy.
Some punctuation/context collisions retain multiple print spellings after semantic context is known; they need a canonicalization or ambiguity policy.
29 no-cell forward rules require an explicit reconstruction contract rather than blind inversion.
Multi-cell and sequence signatures require longest-match / segmentation rules.
Reverse conformance must be authored independently and should include ambiguity, state transitions, malformed Braille, and round-trip properties.
